subject: Preflight: Telemetry-gateway for encrypted egress (HSM/BYOK constraints)
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@primecloud.io>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acme-health.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry + BYOK gateway — can we preflight constraints?

Hey Rishi — thanks again for the quick intro yesterday. Two follow-ups from our engineering and security teams as we scope Private (VPC) onboarding: 

1) We need an encrypted-egress path for operator telemetry. All telemetry leaving our VPC to Redwood's control plane must be wrapped by customer-held keys (BYOK) in an HSM-backed envelope (we use CloudHSM).
2) Telemetry must be scrubbed of PII at the edge and signed with an ephemeral key before it crosses the subnet.
3) We cannot expose any long-term key material to Redwood-managed services; only attestations and wrapped blobs (RSA-OAEP / AES-KW) are allowed.

Attached is a short doc with network egress rules and allowed header fields — can you confirm Redwood supports an HSM-escrow gateway pattern or suggest an alternative? We have an internal SLO for the telemetry pipeline of 99.95% and would like to understand performance implications.

Thanks,
Daniel
---
Daniel Park
Principal Infra Engineer, PrimeCloud
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@primecloud.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry + BYOK gateway — can we preflight constraints?

Hi Daniel — appreciate the detail. Quick summary of what Redwood can offer and open questions: 

- Pattern: We can support an egress proxy that accepts blinded/wrapped telemetry blobs from customer VMs and forwards them to our control plane. The proxy can verify a remote attestation and only accept AES-KW-wrapped payloads. We keep no unwrapped key material.
- HSM integration: We support verifying HSM attestations (PKCS#11/JWT-based) and can accept RSA-OAEP-encrypted CEK blocks. We do not perform key ceremony for those CEKs — Redwood stores only the wrapped CEKs.
- Telemetry signing: We can accept ephemeral signatures for integrity (ECDSA), generated by a short-lived key material managed in your HSM.

Open items we need to confirm with your team:
- Do you require Redwood to perform any unwrapping for parsing telemetry (e.g., to run high-cardinality metrics pipelines)? If so, we need a declaration of allowed metadata fields that may be unwrapped for indexing.
- Bandwidth/SLO tradeoff: can you share the expected telemetry QPS and average blob sizes? That will determine whether the gateway needs to be colocated with a dedicated GPU/CPU pool for cryptographic ops or if it can be a lightweight sidecar.

I've looped in Marissa (Security) and Tessa (Ops) to work through the attestation and deployment checklist. I'll draft a preflight architecture note and share a diagram.

Best,
Rishi

Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, Daniel Park <daniel.park@primecloud.io>
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry + BYOK gateway — can we preflight constraints?

Thanks — attaching an initial sketch and a short checklist (see attachments). Key decisions and recommendations from Security: 

- Recommendation A (Operatorless-wrapping): PrimeCloud performs full field-level scrubbing + wraps the telemetry CEK with your HSM. Redwood ingests the wrapped blob and stores it as an opaque telemetry document. No unwrapping at Redwood. This is simplest for compliance but limits our ability to do structured indexing.
- Recommendation B (Indexing proxy opt-in): PrimeCloud marks non-PII fields to be unwrapped. To support indexing, Redwood would perform unwrapping inside a short-lived ephemeral JIT enclave that uses a customer-provided unwrapping token (audited). Unwrapping must be explicit for each field; we log all operations to an immutable audit stream.

Operational notes:
- We can provide two deployment patterns: (1) Sidecar gateway deployed into your telemetry subnets (recommended for <2k QPS) or (2) Dedicated egress nodes behind a private cross-connect for higher throughput.
- Telemetry signature verification is O(1) per blob; wrapping/unwrapping is the heavier op. Expect ~5–12ms per CEK unwrap on typical CloudHSM hardware; if you have 50K blobs/sec that pushes us to dedicated hardware.

Action items for PrimeCloud engineers:
- Share a sample telemetry blob (anonymized) and QPS profile.
- Confirm whether any downstream Redwood feature requires structured access to the telemetry payloads.

Attachments: telemetry-proxy-v1.drawio.png (diagram), primecloud-egress-constraints-20260911.pdf (their doc)

—
Marissa Cole
Security Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@primecloud.io>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry + BYOK gateway — can we preflight constraints?

Marissa / Rishi — thanks for the clear options. PrimeCloud is comfortable with Recommendation B (Indexing proxy opt-in) provided: 

- Unwrapping only occurs inside an auditable ephemeral enclave in our VPC, not in any multi-tenant Redwood pool.
- Redwood must provide a signed audit record (SHA256 digest + timestamp + run-id) for each unwrapping event that we can ingest into our SIEM.
- Performance target: latency budget for telemetry ingestion overall should remain <50ms  p95 for the path between sidecar and Redwood indexing (we can accept up to 8ms overhead for unwrap).

We'll produce an anonymized sample blob and QPS numbers by Wednesday. Next step from Redwood: a short SOW addendum that documents the unwrapping contract and required audit fields. If you can send a draft SOW addendum and a small perf test plan, we'll put the procurement team on a quick review.

Thanks,
Daniel

Daniel Park
Principal Infra Engineer, PrimeCloud
